caveats: Guarantee covers only the Gaussian measurements listed in entries.
Public vocabulary (map ids, H3 cells) is assumed data-independent.

Contribution capping is per-user deterministic, so it is covered by the clipping bound; stay-point/map-matching steps run per user and add no leakage beyond that bound if their parameters are fixed in advance.
Hyperparameters (caps, sigma, tau) were not tuned on private data unless stated; any such tuning is NOT accounted.
Floating-point Gaussian sampling is not hardened against floating-point attacks.

Parameters informed by real data (non-DP, not accounted): outing gap 2 h, real-outing rule (>=5 min, >=500 m), minimum activity (>=10 outings on >=5 days), stop rule 200 m / 10 min, the place-snap radius (150 m, raised from 75 m after seeing the snap rate), the time bins (4 tod x weekday/weekend in the tokenizer, coarse am/pm x weekday/weekend in the released tables), the H3 hierarchy resolutions (place 6-7-8, traversal 6-7), and the per-user caps (100 outings, 50 res-8 stop cells, 1000 res-8 traversed cells). They were chosen from the outings EDA run on the real data.
Histogram bin edges and the per-table per-user key caps (place m=12/25/50, traversal m=20/100) were chosen after looking at the EDA quantiles of the real data (not accounted).

Declared design choices fixed before any SNR was computed: place-tier priorities [6.0, 3.0, 1.0], traversal-tier priorities [3.0, 2.0], refine thresholds tau place [2.0, 2.0] / traversal [2.0] (in sigma units of the parent's noisy value) and a 40% equal-split floor. rho weights use public quantities only (table sensitivity^2, public vocabulary size, priority).
Floating-point Gaussian sampling (numpy) is not hardened against floating-point attacks.

Per-user processing (outing subsampling seeded from the user's pseudonym, top-m key truncation, L1 normalisation, stop detection and snapping upstream) is a deterministic function of that user's data alone, so the stated sensitivities hold; the tokenizer's behaviour is assumed to have the same property.
Child tiers are released only under parents whose NOISY count passed tau*sigma (post-processing); when a tier's vocabulary is empty its planned rho is still charged (conservative).
Tables are sums of per-user pmfs (user-weighted); user-level histograms are one-hot per user (L2 = 1), computed on uncapped per-user statistics.

outing_detour is a proxy (route length / distance between first and last visit cell centres, only when that distance >= 2 km, quantised at about 0.5 km); outing_mode comes from labels available for a subset of users and is mostly 'unknown'.

DATA-DEPENDENT DESIGN CHOICE (outside the formal DP guarantee): the table list (which tables were dropped: place_time_users, stop_transitions_r6, trav_users_r8, trav_users_r9) and the coarse time bins (am [05,14) / pm [14,05) local, 2 x 2) were chosen after looking at the signal-to-noise of a previous run on the real data. The final mechanism's DP guarantee is therefore conditional on this data-dependent design choice, which is not accounted for.
Within-coarse-bin split of time mass into the 4 fine bins (schema_v2.COARSE_TO_FINE) is a fixed assumption (uniform over local hours), not measured.
Co-visit degree histogram not released (sensitivity would depend on other users' data).

Sensor statistics (sampling interval, gap rate, noise, speeds) are NOT measured: UserOutings carries no raw points, and measuring them user-level would need extra tables; the artifact 'generation' dict leaves the generator defaults.
